props.name: dismissible
props.description: Closes when the backdrop is clicked.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the panel. The consumer's title slot supplies it best.

props.name: modal
props.description: Modal is the default: the page behind is inert and focus is trapped. A non-modal drawer is for a persistent side panel the reader keeps open while working.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the drawer is showing. Reflects so page CSS can target it.

props.name: show
props.description: Opens the drawer. Equivalent to setting `open`.

props.name: side
props.description: Which edge it slides from.  Both values are logical and mirror under `dir="rtl"`, which is ADR-016's requirement. There is no physical pair — see the note at the top of the stylesheet for why.

ai.summary: A panel that slides in from one edge, for navigation or a persistent side task.
whenToUse: Navigation or filters live beside the content rather than over it
The panel stays open while the reader works — a non-modal side panel
The content is taller than it is wide, such as a menu or a filter list
whenNotToUse: It must interrupt and demand a decision — use a Dialog or Alert Dialog
The content is a short description of a control — use a Tooltip
The content is a small menu anchored to a button — use a Popover
ai.accessibility: Reuses the dialog mechanics in `shared/dialog-base.ts`, so the native `<dialog>` owns focus trapping, Escape, `::backdrop`, and inert background content — nothing is reimplemented. Focus returns to the trigger on close. `side` is logical: `start` and `end` mirror under `dir="rtl"` (ADR-016), and there is deliberately no physical `left`/`right` pair, because a fixed edge is exactly what puts a drawer on the wrong side of a right-to-left document.
knownLimitations: The panel needs an `[hidden][open]` rule: scoped mode writes `hidden` onto elements hosting a `<slot>`, which otherwise leaves an open drawer invisible
No physical side values — see the accessibility note
